label: X-ray · pneumothorax
how: Look for a thin white visceral pleural line with no lung markings outside it. On an upright film the air rises to the apex. Do not call skin folds; a fold has markings beyond the line.
title: Chest X-ray of pneumothorax.png

label: X-ray · pneumonia
how: Look for a focal white airspace opacity. Air bronchograms are dark branching airways inside the white lung. Use the silhouette sign: loss of the heart border means the opacity is in the adjacent lobe.
title: Pneumonia x-ray.jpg

label: X-ray · pleural effusion
how: Compare both costophrenic angles. Fluid blunts the angle and forms a meniscus that is higher laterally. A large effusion pushes the mediastinum away and hides the hemidiaphragm.
title: Two-view chest radiograph depicting bilateral pleural effusions.webp

label: X-ray · small-bowel obstruction
how: On an upright film, look for dilated small-bowel loops and air-fluid levels at different heights. Valvulae conniventes cross the full width of the loop. Do not stop at the film; CT is used to find the transition point.
title: Upright X-ray demonstrating small bowel obstruction.jpg

label: X-ray · rib fracture
how: Trace each rib cortex. A fracture is a break, step-off, or callus. Old fractures show remodeling, not a sharp acute line. Also look under the fracture for pneumothorax or effusion.
title: Chest X-ray of a normal lung with old left 5th and 6th ribs fractures.jpg

label: X-ray · hip
how: Follow Shenton's line along the inferior femoral neck and superior obturator foramen. A break in that arc, or a shortened externally rotated hip, raises concern for a femoral-neck fracture.
title: Plain radiograph of the right hip .jpg

label: X-ray · Colles fracture
how: A Colles fracture is a distal radial fracture with dorsal angulation, often after a fall on an outstretched hand. Check the radial inclination, the ulnar styloid, and the radiocarpal joint.
title: ZP fraktura collesova (32).jpg

label: X-ray · prior tuberculosis
how: Upper-lobe fibrotic scar and volume loss suggest healed secondary tuberculosis. Calcified nodes or a Ghon focus can remain. This is not the same as active disease; activity needs comparison and clinical context.
title: Chest x-ray of distinct fibrotic scar after secondary tuberculosis.jpg

label: CT · paranasal sinuses
how: On a coronal bone window, name maxillary, ethmoid, and frontal sinuses. Mucosa is a thin soft-tissue line. Thickening, an air-fluid level, or obstruction of the ostiomeatal complex is the finding to describe.
title: Coronal plane CT scan of the paranasal sinuses illustrative image.jpg

label: CT · stroke
how: On a non-contrast head CT, acute blood is bright. Early ischemia is subtle: loss of gray-white distinction, sulcal effacement, or a hyperdense artery. A normal early CT does not exclude stroke.
title: Brain CT Scan for Stroke Diagnosis.jpg

label: CT · brain mass
how: Find the mass, then say which side and which compartment. Look for surrounding low-density edema, midline shift, and whether ventricles are compressed. This frame is a teaching CT, not a full MRI workup.
title: TAC Brain tumor glioblastoma-Coronal plane.gif

label: CT · lung nodule
how: Use lung windows. A nodule is a round opacity. Calcification that is central or diffuse is more often benign. Size, margin, and comparison with an older CT decide the next step.
title: CT-Standard-Dose-2.50-Lung-Calcified-Nodule.jpg

label: CT · appendicitis
how: Find the cecum, then the blind-ending appendix. Appendicitis shows a dilated appendix, wall thickening, and periappendiceal fat stranding. Look for an appendicolith and for free air or abscess.
title: Contrast-enhanced CT scan (coronal) of abdomen and pelvis showing acute appendicitis.jpg
